incident-bot: [INCIDENT] P2 — alert flood: ~620 alerts in 8m for alertname="inference_overload" service=model-serving; auto-paged oncall
Priya Singh: I'm looking. Can someone confirm customer-facing errors?
Omar Khalid: Seeing 5xx rate up across 3 customers (api keys a, b, c). Error traces show worker queue full + connection reset.
Ben Park: Logs show worker OOM kills are NOT happening, it's request queue saturation at the runtime layer. Likely new model rollout increased per-request memory temporarily.
Robert Yang: We're 90% through a staged model push. New config bumped batch_size default to 8 -> 16 on a subset of nodes. That doubled request working set for some nodes.
Priya Singh: Ok immediate plan: 1) throttle PD notifications for identical signatures 2) add short-lived grouping by fingerprint (model_version + node id) and set repeat interval 15m 3) deploy runtime config to cap batch_size to 10 on affected nodes 4) create temp dashboard and followup ticket. Agree?
Karen Li: +1. Please scope any suppression to service=model-serving and model_version=2026-03-15-v2 so we don't silence unrelated alerts.
SRE-AutoBot: Suggested action — apply Alertmanager silence for matching labels.
Priya Singh: Omar, can you paste the silence command you'll apply? I want it in the incident log.
Omar Khalid: Running (10m):
```
alertmanager silence add --match 'alertname="inference_overload", service="model-serving", model_version="2026-03-15-v2"' --author='Omar' --duration=10m --comment='suppress duplicate PD for model rollout spike'
```
Ben Park: Also adding a temporary webhook throttle on PD for this service: 5 notifications/min for matching fingerprints.
PagerDuty Bot: PagerDuty override created: override_id=ovr-55221 scope=service:model-serving model_version=2026-03-15-v2 duration=10m
Priya Singh: For longer-term we should fingerprint alerts. Proposed fingerprint formula: sha1(alertname + '|' + model_version + '|' + node). That would group identical heap of alerts into single PD incident and reduce noise.
Robert Yang: Agreed. Here's a sample group_by route patch to roll out as a 1% canary then 100% if green:
```yaml
route:
  group_by: ['alertname', 'model_version', 'fingerprint']
  group_interval: 30s
  repeat_interval: 15m
  receiver: 'pd_main'
```
Priya Singh: Also increasing alert 'for' clause on the Prometheus rule to 3m to avoid firing on short transient spikes. See rule edit below.
Priya Singh: ```yaml
- alert: inference_overload
  expr: rate(inference_errors_total[1m]) > 50
  for: 3m
  labels:
    severity: page
  annotations:
    summary: 'Inference service overload ({{ $labels.instance }})'
```
Ben Park: Runtime change deployed to cap batch_size 10 on the rollout shard group — canary in 2 nodes first. DevDeployBot: config model-runtime@2026-03-15-batchcap canary started
SRE-AutoBot: Temp Grafana created: https://grafana.redwood/d/ops/temp-model-overload-2270001234
Omar Khalid: After throttling PD and capping batch size, error rate dropped ~65% in 6m. Latency tail improving.
Priya Singh: Good. Creating follow-up ticket TICKET-4412 — "model-serving: alert dedupe, grouping, and notification-rate-limits". Includes ops docs, runbook changes, and a config change to compute fingerprint labels. Assigning to eng-sre + eng-runtime.
Priya Singh: I'll schedule a 45m post-incident tuning meeting tomorrow to land permanent changes and review runbook edits. Handoff to night oncall in 30m — @Karen please take over monitoring and ensure silence id + ticket link are in the handoff note.
Karen Li: Taking handoff. Please drop silence id and PD override id in the handoff doc. I'll follow up with eng-runtime tomorrow morning to set permanent caps if needed.
PagerDuty Bot: Silence applied id=sil-112233 scope=service:model-serving model_version=2026-03-15-v2 duration=10m
Priya Singh: Notes added to incident doc, links: dashboard, runbook snippet, TICKET-4412. Thanks everyone for quick moves. :clap:
incident-bot: Incident P2 — mitigations applied (silence, PD override, batch cap canary). Next: post-incident tuning meeting and runbook updates. Status: monitoring."
